contentText: Syllabus (GS3):  Equity instruments, shares/IPO/DEMAT, SENSEX, mutual funds, ETF, derivatives (F&O), commodity market. 1. Equity & Early-Stage Investors Equity holders = owners; get dividend only if there is profit; last (residual) claim on liquidation. Private Equity (PE):  fund investing in private UNLISTED companies (Byju's, Parle). Venture Capital Fund (VCF):  PE sub-type giving seed capital to start-ups. Angel investor:  rich individual funding start-ups (e.g. Ratan Tata). Corporate Strategic investor:  invests to acquire the company/tech later. 2. Share Types Q - Preference vs Ordinary shares? Preference share Ordinary (equity) share Fixed dividend rate (e.g. 10%) Dividend fluctuates with profit left over Paid before ordinary holders on liquidation; NO voting rights Paid after preference holders; HAS voting rights Can be converted to ordinary; lower risk Cannot be converted; higher risk Sweat/Sweet Equity, ESOP:  shares at discount to directors/employees for value added. By quality:  Penny stock (junk co, very low price), Blue-chip (strong co - Reliance/TCS), Multibagger (rapid rise - IRCTC 2021), Cyclical/seasonal (auto shares in festival season). Floating vs Restricted:  whether shares are freely tradable in the secondary market. 3. Accounts, Valuation & Ratios Account types:  Personal (person/company), Real (tangible + intangible like goodwill/patent), Nominal (income/expense). Goodwill:  intangible asset = price paid ABOVE fair value of a target's assets (its brand/reputation). Market cap  = total shares x current price. Unicorn = start-up valued >= $1 billion. EBITDA  = Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation & Amortization.  Depreciation  = wear of physical assets;  Amortization  = fall in value of intangibles. Net worth  = total assets - total liabilities (can be negative, e.g. Anil Ambani's Reliance Capital). Q - Small / Mid / Large Cap? Cap category (SEBI rank) Feature Large Cap (top-100 by market cap) Low risk, high liquidity (Reliance, TCS, Infosys) Mid Cap (rank 101-250) Medium risk & liquidity (Castrol) Small Cap (below rank 250) High risk, low liquidity Records:  Reliance = 1st Indian co to hit Rs.20 lakh cr market cap (2024); NVIDIA = 1st to hit $5 trillion (2025). Market froth / asset bubble:  investors ignore fundamentals -> unsustainable price rise -> collapse (Dotcom 2001, Subprime 2007-08).  Tulip Mania  = 1600s Holland; term for irrational manias.  Volatility/ViX  = speed of price swings.  Key-Man Risk  = over-dependence on one person (Elon Musk). P/E ratio & EPS, Debt-to-Equity ratio:  used to compare companies (Tata Motors D/E ~2 vs debt-free Maruti ~0). 4. Issuing & Selling Shares Face value  = printed value; sold above = 'premium', below = 'discount'.  Prospectus  = IPO document;  Guidance  = company's growth estimate. IPO  = 1st public share issue;  FPO  = later issue;  Rights issue  = FPO with first right to existing holders;  QIP  = shares only to Qualified Institutional Buyers (SBI's Rs.25,000 cr QIP, 2025, largest);  Private placement  = to select investors. Underwriter (Lead Manager):  merchant banker who issues the IPO and buys unsold shares. Grey market / 'kerb trading':  unofficial trading before listing; SEBI's 'when-listed' platform aims to formalize it. OFS  (owner sells his own shares) vs  Open Offer ;  Bonus shares  (free extra shares -> average price falls);  Share split ;  Buyback  (company repurchases its shares). ADR / GDR:  a non-US company deposits shares with a US bank, which issues American/Global Depositary Receipts to foreign investors (avoids registering with US SEBI).  IDR  = same for a non-Indian company in India. Direct listing  of Indian firms abroad allowed via GIFT City (2023).  ICO  (Initial Coin Offering for crypto) prohibited by FinMin's FIU (2026). 5. Stock Exchanges, DEMAT & CCP Exchanges:  world's oldest = Amsterdam (1602); Asia's oldest = BSE (1875). Platforms: BOLT (BSE), NEAT (NSE). Social Stock Exchange (Budget-2019):  under SEBI, lets NGOs/NPOs raise funds for social projects (via Zero Coupon Zero Principal instruments). DEMAT & Depositories:  hold securities electronically (dematerialized). SEBI regulates under Depositories Act 1996. Two: CDSL (owned by BSE) and NSDL (owned by NSE/SBI). PAN mandatory for DEMAT (post-Rupal Panchal scam). ASBA:  Application Supported by Blocked Amount - IPO money only debited if shares allotted (investor earns interest meanwhile); UPI-ASBA extended to secondary market (2024). ISIN  = 12-char code identifying a security.  CAS  = monthly consolidated account statement emailed by depositories. Central Counterparty (CCP):  sits between buyer & seller ('novation') so if one defaults, the CCP honours the trade (prevents system failure). e.g. Clearing Corporation of India. CCP regulator For RBI (PSS Act 2007) Money transfer between buyer & seller RBI (FEMA 1999) Foreign-currency transactions SEBI (SEBI Act 1992, SCRA 1956) Shares, bonds, commodities 6. Investor Types & Indices By capacity:  Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIB - mutual funds, insurers); Anchor investors (QIB sub-type offered shares pre-IPO); Retail investors. By behaviour:  Jobber (own money), STAG (buys IPO to flip), Bull (expects rise, buys), Bear (expects fall, sells). Disposition effect:  sell winners fast but hold losers too long. Trading styles: margin, intraday, swing, long-term, block deal, contra. Q - SENSEX vs NIFTY vs Nikkei? SENSEX:  BSE index of 30 companies (free-float market cap weighted). NIFTY:  NSE index of 50 companies.  Nikkei:  Tokyo exchange index of 225. SENSEX rises:  soft monetary policy, peace/boom, higher FDI limit, mergers. Falls: tight policy, war/recession, scandals. Force Majeure:  'superior force' - unforeseeable events (disaster, war, epidemic) excuse a party from a contract. Market snapshot (ES25):  India = 4th-largest equity market (2024, after US/China/Japan). FPI exits hurt less now (Indian investors absorb the shares). India-US link (Granger causality): if US market falls, India usually falls (21/22 times); reverse not true - Indian markets react more to US trends. Efficient Market Hypothesis / Random Walk:  prices already reflect all info & move unpredictably, so no one can consistently beat the market. Beta  = a share's volatility vs the market (>1 = moves faster, <1 = slower, <0 = opposite like gold).  Alpha  = a fund's return vs benchmark (SENSEX). Fundamental  (profit/balance sheet - long-term investors) vs  Technical  analysis (price charts - traders). 7. SEBI Anti-Scam & Market Safety Circuit breaker:  halts trading if a price swing exceeds x% (after Harshad Mehta 1992, Ketan Parekh 2001). Settlement:  Badla/carry-forward banned (2001) -> rolling settlement T+2 -> now T+1, moving to T+1 hour / T+0 (instant). Illegal trading:  Dabba trading (off-books), Insider trading (using confidential info), Front running (broker trades ahead of client order) - all banned. Investor Protection Fund (IPF):  covers non-speculative losses up to Rs.25 lakh.  Settlement Guarantee Fund (SGF)  similar. Server safety:  SEBI's Business Continuity Plan + Disaster Recovery Site; LAMA (IT monitoring); IRRA portal (close trades during glitches). Adani-Hindenburg (2023):  'flash crash' after fraud allegations;  Short selling  = borrow-sell-rebuy-cheaper to profit from a fall.  Finfluencers  - SEBI penalises wrong financial advice. Arbitrage:  profit from price gaps across markets.  Bid-Ask spread  (high spread = low liquidity).  Yen carry trade  unwind (2024) caused a global market fall. 8. G-Sec Trading Platforms Retail Direct Scheme / RDG (2021):  retail investors (& NRIs) buy T-Bill/G-Sec/SDL/SGB directly from RBI on E-Kuber (no MF commission) -> deepens the G-Sec market. NDS-OM:  RBI's electronic, anonymous, order-matching platform for G-Sec (maintained by CCIL); also telephone & OTC modes. E-Kuber:  RBI's core banking platform (NEFT/RTGS, Repo, CRR, G-Sec, SGB, RDG). 9. Investment Funds Mutual Fund (for aam-aadmi):  an AMC pools retail savings, gives 'units', invests in a portfolio; charges entry/exit load. Types: Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Multi-asset. Open vs Close ended:  unlimited/anytime vs fixed size/maturity.  Lumpsum vs SIP  (systematic monthly).  ESG/Shariah  funds;  ELSS  (3-yr lock, tax benefit);  ULIP  (MF + insurance);  Risk-o-meter  (6 risk levels). Hedge Fund (for rich):  HNI-only, min Rs.1 crore; high-risk (junk bonds, arbitrage, F&O). REIT / InvIT:  trusts investing in real estate (min Rs.50k) / infrastructure like highways-airports (min Rs.1 lakh); SEBI-permitted 2014. Sovereign Wealth Fund:  state-owned investment fund (Abu Dhabi ADIA, Singapore GIC, Qatar QIA). Q - CPSE-ETF vs Index-ETF vs Mutual Fund? Fund Nature CPSE-ETF / Bharat Bond ETF Bundles Govt-company shares/bonds - a disinvestment/borrowing tool; fixed portfolio. Index-ETF (passive) Mechanically tracks an index; low fees, high liquidity, resellable. Mutual Fund (active) Manager actively picks securities; higher fees. Bitcoin ETF:  approved in USA (2024, by SEC); not in India. Overseas-ETF: SEBI capped Indian MF investment at $1 bn (FEMA), paused inflows 2024. Gold ETF  (SEBI-regulated, resellable) vs  Digital Gold apps  (unregulated - SEBI warns, 2025). Alternative Investment Funds (AIF):  Cat-I (positive spillover - VC, angel, infra, SME; light norms), Cat-II (PE/debt), Cat-III (high-risk - hedge funds; strict norms). 10. Derivatives, F&O & Commodity Market Forward/Future contract:  buy/sell on a future date at a price fixed today.  Option  (Call/Put) = right (not obligation) to execute; buying it =  hedging  (risk protection). Derivative:  value derived from an underlying asset (share/bond/commodity/currency).  Swap  = exchange one asset/cash flow for another (Currency swap, Credit Default Swap). Over-financialisation (ES24/25):  financial sector too big vs real economy (India market-cap 140% of GDP, 2024) -> instability, inequality, talent drain; a 'bell-shaped' link with GDP growth. Sachetisation of F&O (ES24):  cheap access lets the poor gamble; SEBI says 9 of 10 F&O traders lose money.  Jane Street  - US prop-firm fined for Rs.4000+ cr F&O manipulation. P-Notes (Participatory Notes):  offshore derivative issued by a SEBI-registered FPI to a foreign investor who doesn't want to register with SEBI -> risk of tax evasion / laundering; SEBI tightening.  Bharat-DR  = reverse (foreign co selling to Indians without SEBI registration). Commodity market:  regulated by Forward Market Commission -> FMC merged into SEBI (2015, after Jignesh Shah's NSEL scam). Gold:  Gold exchanges (SEBI regulates; WDRA does warehousing); Electronic Gold Receipts (EGR); India International Bullion Exchange (IIBX, GIFT City, 2022 - 1st bullion exchange). Tax relief GIVEN on:  5-yr tax-saver FD, PPF/EPF/SSY/NSC, NPS, ELSS, tax-free bonds (NHAI/IRFC/PFC/HUDCO), donations, GIFT City investments. Tax relief NOT given on:  savings-account interest, Sovereign Green Bonds, G-Sec/T-Bill, shares/company bonds, F&O, P-Notes, MF/REIT/ETF, crypto (30%), property/gold. RGESS (2012) gave first-time equity investors relief (ended 2017). Key Facts (Quick Revision) Fact Detail Preference vs Ordinary Fixed dividend, no vote, paid first vs variable, votes, paid last. Market cap ranks (SEBI) Large = top 100; Mid = 101-250; Small = below 250. ADR/GDR Non-US co shares via US bank to foreign investors (no US-SEBI registration). P-Notes Offshore derivative by FPI; foreign investor avoids SEBI registration. SENSEX / NIFTY BSE-30 / NSE-50 indices. Retail Direct (2021) Buy G-Sec directly from RBI (E-Kuber). REIT / InvIT (2014) Real estate / infrastructure investment trusts. FMC -> SEBI (2015) Commodity-market regulator merged into SEBI. IIBX (2022) India's 1st bullion exchange, GIFT City. Hedge Fund / AIF Cat-III High-risk, HNI (min Rs.1 cr). Practice PYQs (attached PDF) UPSC/CDS/IES/EPFO PYQs - full question, options and answer with reasoning - are in the attached PDF below.
